title: Comparison of global cohomology
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme and $\Lambda$ a finite discrete ring, with left $\Lambda$-module sheaves. For $K\in\Dplus(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], the unit $\eta_K:K	o R
u_{T,*}
u_T^*K$ of the bounded-below derived comparison adjunction [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] induces a natural isomorphism
$$
 R\Gamma(T_{\Et},K)\xrightarrow{\sim}
 R\Gamma(T_{\Proet},
u_T^*K).
$$
This is the composite of $R\Gamma(T_{\Et},\eta_K)$ with the canonical final-object comparison $R\Gamma(T_{\Et},R
u_{T,*}
u_T^*K)\cong R\Gamma(T_{\Proet},
u_T^*K)$ [lem-weil-pbc-derived-sections-pushforward]. Both section functors are ordinary right-derived sections at the terminal objects, with the etale construction of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

proof.text: Let G and G' be evaluation at the terminal étale and pro-étale objects, and let e be the displayed adjunction-unit evaluation. The finite-level comparison proposition gives finite-limit and finite-colimit preservation for the comparison inverse image. Its ordinary adjunction unit is invertible by the comparison full-faithfulness theorem. The generic bounded-below right-derived base-change theorem therefore applies once the pro-étale terminal evaluation of every pulled-back injective is right-acyclic.

source.place: Proof paragraph: exact comparison inverse image and the derived unit.

proof.text: The terminal-evaluation acyclicity is the global-sections comparison lemma: for every injective étale module sheaf I, all positive right-derived global sections of its comparison pullback vanish. Applying Functor.isIso_rightDerivedFunctorPlusBaseChange_of_rightAcyclic to e gives the isomorphism of the bounded-below derived evaluation functors, which is definitionally the finiteComparisonGlobalSections transformation.

statement_change.what: The text only said finite Lambda, without introducing its ring structure or the left-module convention. The recorded etale coefficient definition is commutative-ring-valued, while the finite-level comparison and its source context allow arbitrary finite rings and left modules. The corrected text explicitly fixes that coefficient convention and specifies the previously unnamed canonical final-object comparison used after the derived unit, adding its existing DAG node to statement dependencies. This changes no mathematical hypothesis relative to the source context and imposes no commutativity assumption.
